LESSON: MANAGEMENT OF SOLID WASTE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four
Subject: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Matter 2.1 Properties of matter (14 lessons) ● Meaning of matter ● States of mat
Topic 2.2: Management of solid waste
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 16

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Management of solid waste, part of Matter 2.1 Properties of matter (14 lessons) ● Meaning of matter ● States of mat in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade four SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How is solid waste dangerous to the environment?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Identify solid waste in the environment with peers. Learners with speech difficulties could use alternative and augmentative modes of communication during discussion with peers.
2. Discuss in purposive pairs the meaning of decomposable and non-decomposable solid waste.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Management of solid waste together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: The learner reflects on ways of managing different types of waste in their

environment.

● Creativity and imagination: The learner explores ways of making dust bins for safe disposal of waste at home and in school

using locally available materials.

Values:
Responsibility: The learner uses proper safety measures in solid waste management. (wearing protective gears and use of

appropriate tools)

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Health issues (preventive health): The learner discusses the dangers of solid waste to the environment and presents in class.

 Socio-economic issues (environmental education): The learner discusses ways of managing different types of solid waste in

their environment.

Link to other Learning area:

Creative arts: The learner uses knowledge on management of solid waste to make ornaments and dustbins.
